evidence.note: Claim: bug found --globs naming a file that exists nowhere is accepted silently (the fix task keeps the glob verbatim and the reply carries no warning). Mechanism: fix_task_globs returns explicit globs verbatim; bug_found reply has no glob_warnings field. Refuting observation: on unfixed code, out.data.get('glob_warnings') is None for a --globs naming an absent file. Verified in-process: UNFIXED -> glob_warnings None (assertion fails); FIXED -> glob_warnings ['src/guessed/standards.py names no tracked file']. Claim CONFIRMED.

Read the governing rules: r-task-phase-needs-wave (fix task carries no-deps tag), r-gemini-key-load (export GEMINI_API_KEY before gemini review), r-ddflow-self-assessment; decisions D-dx-plan-globs-exist (missing-glob is a warning, never a refusal) and the fix keeps the loud-flag never-refuse shape.

Implemented missing_loud(root, globs) in ddflow/api/knowledge/bugs.py: one warning per literal glob naming no tracked file and not already on disk; bug_found surfaces glob_warnings; CLI (surfaces/commands/bug_found.py) and MCP (surfaces/declared/records.py payload) carry it. Regression test tests/test_fix_task_globs_exist.py::test_an_explicit_glob_naming_no_file_is_loudly_flagged fails on unfixed code and passes after.

chunk_findings.detail: `missing_loud` never tests membership in `GIT.files(..., "tracked")`. It only uses that list for hints, and it skips any path for which `(root / rel).exists()` is true. Given `--globs src/real.py` where `src/real.py` is tracked but deleted from the worktree, `exists()` is false and the result is `"'src/real.py' names no tracked file"`, which is false. Given `--globs build/artifact.py` where that path exists on disk but is untracked and was not declared new, `exists()` is true so there is no warning and the fix task is still filed with that glob — the same silent wrong lease as Bf839186cee, just with a stray on-disk path instead of a missing one. The stated check is “no tracked file, and not declared new,” not “missing from the worktree.”

chunk_findings.detail: `rel in tracked` is a raw string compare after only `lstrip("/")`, so a glob that names a tracked file under another spelling is reported as missing. Given tracked `src/real.py` and `--globs ./src/real.py` (or `src/foo/../real.py`, or an absolute path to that file), `(root / rel)` still points at the tracked file but `rel` is not an element of `GIT.files(..., "tracked")`, so the function returns `"'./src/real.py' names no tracked file"`. That contradicts the new contract that a tracked path is in scope regardless of how the worktree path is written.

chunk_findings.detail: The new setup commits `src/real.py` and leaves it on disk, then still files `src/real.py` plus a path that exists nowhere. On that input the old `(root / rel).exists()` check and the new tracked-membership check emit the same warnings, so this test passes on the unfixed code. It never deletes a tracked file from the worktree, and it never passes an on-disk untracked path, which are the two cases the docstring claims to lock.

chunk_findings.detail: `normpath(raw.lstrip("/"))` only folds relative spellings (`./src/real.py`, `src/foo/../real.py`). An absolute glob of the same tracked file is still a raw string compare against `GIT.files(..., "tracked")`. Given tracked `src/real.py` and `--globs [REDACTED:path]` (repo root `[REDACTED:path]`), `lstrip("/")` yields `home/proj/src/real.py`, which is not an element of the tracked list, so the function still returns `"'[REDACTED:path]' names no tracked file"`. That is the absolute-path half of the prior membership finding; the new comment that a tracked file is in scope however it is spelled is false for that input.

chunk_findings.detail: The new host-absolute strip compares `os.path.normpath(raw)` to `root.resolve().as_posix()`, which are not the same spelling of a path. Given a tracked `src/real.py`, repo root `Path("[REDACTED:path]")` where that path is a symlink to `/var/repos/proj` (or `/home` itself is a symlink), and `--globs [REDACTED:path]`, `resolve()` yields `/var/repos/proj` so the prefix test fails, the leading-slash branch then turns the glob into `home/me/proj/src/real.py`, and that string is not in `GIT.files(..., "tracked")`, so the function still returns `"'[REDACTED:path]' names no tracked file"` for a tracked file. The same false miss happens on Windows for `C:\proj\src\real.py`: `normpath` keeps backslashes while `as_posix()` does not, so the prefix never matches.

data.probe: Out of contract for missing_loud: globs are repo-relative POSIX paths (git ls-files yields them; a leading slash is the repo-root anchor, see existing_globs). A host-absolute path is itself an unusual input this function defends against only as a convenience; a symlink-resolved-root miss or a Windows separator can at worst emit a wrong ADVISORY warning string, never a wrong lease -- the glob is kept verbatim in every branch. POSIX-only project (posixpath imported throughout; the repo never stores backslash paths).

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression setup runs `git add src/real.py` immediately after `_seed(repo)` and never creates that path. The previous test treated `src/real.py` as a glob naming a file that exists nowhere, so seed does not write it. Given that worktree, `git add` exits 128 (pathspec did not match) and `check=True` raises `CalledProcessError` before `bug_found` or any assertion, so the Bf839186cee case never runs.
